reviews.review:
Holy Snapz, it works again! There was a long stretch of time (after/around the release of Windows 10) where this game wouldn't load. Now it does, and guess what, this game is still incredibly fun, and if you can't tell from my playtime, one of my favorite roguelikes ever. Compared to other roguelikes it does lack some things, such as meaningful level randomization, the warm glow you get from skillfully clearing a room/level without dying (unlike, say, Rogue Legacy), the importance of secret rooms/artifacts after the first time you collect/discover them, etc.

But RoR shines in other areas that heavily outweigh any perceived oversights. The backgrounds and the sense of scale you get from some levels really sets the tone for the game well. The detail put into the minor changes to your character, weapon, or environment you get from pickups is excellent. The depth of character selection and how it affects your gameplay style is second only to Tales of Maj'Eyal (each character isn't just a reskin of the same basic gun, but a completely different way of tackling the game, which in turn restructures which powerups are more important). However, my favorite part of the game is that it has a kind of "achieveable God Mode". Once you find the right artifacts, you can choose your powerups, which, if you play correctly, can lead you to become a one man/woman/robot/alien army of destruction. Which, if you're familiar with roguelikes, barely ever happens. And yet if you're not careful, you can still die on your way to Godhood, so it doesn't feel like you were just handed the keys to seeing all the content.

In conclusion, it's a very well-balanced roguelike, perfect for a quick 30-60min of gameplay, with some good frustrating moments, but also a good chance to fight your way to freedom.

And then feel kind of bad about it ;)

I honestly didn't find this game to be very fun for its price point, even with friends. Roguelikes are one of my less favourable genres personally, so I was no doubt influenced by that. But, generally, I can have fun playing just about any game with friends, and this just...wasn't very fun, no matter how high or low my score went.

One of my all time favorites. Overall great game with excellent mechanics, music and characters. Playing around 10 stages or more in one game sometimes caused low fps but I haven't experienced that in a while so maybe it is fixed. Multiplayer is also a bit of a chore to get working but I have played mostly solo anyway. Strong recommendation, especially if on sale.
Fantastic fun, awesome in every way!
